note: P4341 (Pro 29:6-7) — the evil ensnared in sin, the righteous sing; the righteous know the poor's rights. Two verses.

dims.v: self-entrapment — the evil man caught in his own transgression
the evil man ensnared in his own transgression — sin that traps the sinner, the self-entrapment of wrongdoing, against the righteous who sing free and glad
the righteous joy it is set against (266915)
set against the righteous who sing and rejoice
ra (evil) — 'an EVIL man is ensnared in his transgression'; sin is a snare that catches the sinner (cf 5:22; 1:18). Wrongdoing traps its own author, while the righteous go free.
glad freedom — the righteous who sing and rejoice, unensnared
the singing and rejoicing of the righteous, free from the snare that traps the evil — the glad liberty of a clear conscience, unbound by sin
the evil's entrapment it is set against (266909)
set against the evil ensnared in his transgression
samach (rejoice) — 'but a righteous man SINGS and rejoices'; the righteous, unensnared by sin, are free to sing. A clear conscience is a glad and singing thing (cf 28:1).
compassionate justice — the righteous caring for the cause of the poor
the righteous man's knowing of the rights/cause of the poor — the compassionate concern for justice to the weak that marks the righteous, which the wicked cannot even understand
the wicked's incomprehension it is set against (266922)
set against the wicked who do not understand such concern

yada (know) — 'a righteous man KNOWS the rights of the poor'; the righteous care about justice for the weak, entering into their cause. Concern for the poor is a mark of the righteous heart (cf 31:9; Job 29:16).
callous incomprehension — the wicked blind to concern for the poor
the wicked man's failure to understand the knowledge of the poor's rights — the callous incomprehension that cannot even grasp why the weak should be cared for, the opposite of the righteous concern
the righteous concern it is set against (266917)
set against the righteous who know the poor's rights

bin (understand), negated — 'a wicked man does not understand such knowledge'; the wicked cannot even comprehend concern for the poor. Selfishness blinds a man to the very idea of caring for the weak.
